content: St. John’s Wort, certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) and SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine), and other medications can increase serotonin levels. This may rarely lead to a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or toxicity. If you suspect an overdose and the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can reach poison control at 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. However, it is important to note that this medication may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, cause serotonin syndrome. The risk of this condition is higher if you are taking other drugs that also increase serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the medications you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products. Before taking alosetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications, such as fluvoxamine and viloxazine, may affect the removal of alosetron from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Additionally, the risk of severe constipation complications increases if you are taking other drugs that may cause constipation. For the most accurate and up-to-date information about your medication, always consult your healthcare provider. This document was last revised in May 2024.
